title: Theo and the Echo
premise: Xanthe Eriksen has spent eleven years alone aboard Relay Station Vesper, tending a beacon whose original commissioning orders were scrubbed from every archive. When the colony's children begin dreaming in unison—dreams that carry the beacon's signal—she traces the anomaly to a buried second transmitter and the truth it guards: the beacon is a jury, weighing two cryo-arks of sleeping colonists against each other for the single jump window that can save one ship. The children's shared dream is the beacon's way of forcing a vote no adult was willing to hold. Xanthe must choose between waking her estranged sister's ark or the strangers who raised the children now dreaming of her—and in the end she refuses both options, rewiring the beacon to wake a mixed crew from each ship, accepting exile and a tribunal's judgment so that neither half of humanity is abandoned.
about_author: Juniper Vasquez is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about machines that outlive their makers. She lives off-grid with her partner and an aging satellite dish she refuses to decommission.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Establishes her solitary routine maintaining the beacon on automated Station Vesper, her deliberate invisibility from colony administration, and the small rituals that keep loneliness at bay. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance, cracked by a faint anomalous pulse in the signal.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Idris, a colony schoolteacher, as seven students independently draw identical images: a tower, a red light, a woman's silhouette. He reports it and is dismissed. Emotional beat: unease deepening into conviction that something real is happening.

chapters.title: Maintenance Logs and Ghost Orders
chapters.summary: Xanthe investigates the pulse and finds her own maintenance logs altered—entries she never wrote, referencing a 'Second Voice.' Her isolation suddenly feels engineered. Emotional beat: paranoia; the station she trusted may have been watching her.

chapters.title: The Visitor Who Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: A shuttle arrives carrying Administrator Okonkwo, demanding Xanthe explain power draw spikes. Their charged history—she once loved him, then chose exile at Vesper—resurfaces. Emotional beat: love against duty, first collision; he leaves with questions she refused to answer.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Idris defies orders and brings the dreaming children's drawings to the relay station himself. Xanthe recognizes the tower as her own beacon. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two outsiders finding they are not alone.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Idris locate the buried secondary transmitter beneath the ice shelf. It predates the colony charter. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread—the beacon was never just a lighthouse.

chapters.title: Two Arks
chapters.summary: Decrypted records reveal the truth: two cryo-ships, Halcyon and Meridian, orbiting in dormant drift, and a jump window that can carry only one home. The beacon has been arbitrating for forty years. Emotional beat: vertigo; the colony's entire existence is a waiting room.

chapters.title: Sister, Sleeping
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Xanthe's POV. Her sister Mara boarded Meridian while Xanthe stayed behind—a quarrel over their parents' deaths that became a decade of silence. Emotional beat: grief revealed as the root of her self-imposed exile.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The dream reaches hundreds of children colony-wide; parents panic, the council declares emergency, and Okonkwo moves to seize the station. Emotional beat: rising tension; the secret is slipping beyond anyone's control.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Starlight
chapters.summary: Okonkwo returns with authority to shut down the beacon. Xanthe shows him the arks' telemetry instead of excuses. His duty fractures. Emotional beat: he must choose between his office and the truth—and chooses neither yet.

chapters.title: The Vote Nobody Called
chapters.summary: The children, through the dream-link, begin transmitting a choice back to the beacon: they are voting for Meridian, where their own grandparents sleep. Xanthe realizes the beacon taught them to choose. Emotional beat: horror and wonder entwined.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Council hardliners attempt to destroy the Second Voice before any decision is made public. Xanthe takes a surface crawl through the ice to defend it. Emotional beat: action and sacrifice; she bleeds for the machine she resented.

chapters.title: Waking Mara
chapters.summary: Against protocol, Xanthe opens a comm channel to Meridian and speaks to her sister's cryo-pod's diagnostic system, reading aloud everything she never said. Emotional beat: catharsis; the apology arrives years late but arrives.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Choice
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Ordered to arrest Xanthe, he instead leaks the ark files to the colony. His career ends in real time, and he feels lighter for it. Emotional beat: justice outside the law; love rekindled as partnership rather than opposition.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: Telemetry confirms the jump window begins closing in nine days. The council demands a legal ruling; the beacon demands a human hand on the switch. Both sides arm for confrontation. Emotional beat: ticking clock, dread at maximum.

chapters.title: Tribunal at the Ice Shelf
chapters.summary: Colony assembly convenes at the transmitter itself. Xanthe, Idris, and the children present the dream-evidence. The vote deadlocks exactly along ark lines. Emotional beat: despair; democracy fails where the machine succeeded.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Xanthe realizes the beacon's arbitration logic contains a flaw she can exploit: it can be rewired to split the jump—half capacity to each ark—if someone stays behind to stabilize the relay during transit. That someone must be her. Emotional beat: resolve born from surrender.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Idris and Okonkwo fight her plan; the children, through the dream, endorse it unanimously. Xanthe records farewell messages, including one to Mara that she finally sends. Emotional beat: bittersweet acceptance; found family holding her together as she prepares to let go.

chapters.title: Hand on the Switch
chapters.summary: Climax. During the jump, sabotage from council remnants threatens the split-transit. Xanthe, alone in the core, reroutes power through her own neural-linked console, burning out her implant to hold both arks steady. Emotional beat: white-knuckle sacrifice; the beacon's red light turns white.

chapters.title: Two Ships Home
chapters.summary: Both arks clear the window. On Meridian, Mara wakes to her sister's message and a course set for reunion. On the colony, the children's dreams end gently, leaving only star-charts drawn in crayon. Emotional beat: relief and mourning braided together.

chapters.title: The Echo Answers
chapters.summary: Xanthe survives, implant-scarred and half-deaf, as the beacon transmits its final arbitration: case closed, both ships judged worthy. She steps outside for the first time in twelve years to see two shuttles descending. Emotional beat: grace; the invisible woman becomes the reason everyone survived.

chapters.title: Theo and the Echo
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Idris's POV. A year later, the station is renamed for Theo, the first child who dreamed the beacon's name. Xanthe, no longer hiding, teaches the children the signal's language while Mara rebuilds what the quarrel broke. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the echo finally answered by voices of its own.
